Question ID: GEO_U01_L08_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.FND.1

Which statement best explains why a copied segment is accurate?

answer.text: The compass opening from the original segment was transferred without changing it

feedback.text: Correct. A fixed compass opening preserves the original segment length.

answer.text: The copied segment looks close to the original length

feedback.text: Appearance alone does not prove the segment lengths match.

answer.text: The copied segment was labeled with new letters

feedback.text: Labels name the segment but do not prove equal length.

answer.text: The copied segment was drawn darker than the original

feedback.text: Line darkness is not construction evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U01_L08_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.FND.2

If line line l is the perpendicular bisector of segment AB at point M, which statement must be true?

feedback.text: A bisector creates equal segment parts.

answer.text: AM = MB and line line l forms right angles with AB

feedback.text: Correct. A perpendicular bisector bisects the segment and is perpendicular to it.
A segment length is not equal to a point.

answer.text: Line line l copies angle ABC

feedback.text: A perpendicular bisector is not an angle-copy construction.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U01_L08_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.4

What is the contrapositive of If p, then q?

feedback.text: This is the converse, not the contrapositive.

answer.text: If not p, then not q

feedback.text: This is the inverse, not the contrapositive.

answer.text: If not q, then not p

feedback.text: Correct. The contrapositive switches and negates both parts.
This negates only the conclusion.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U01_L08_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.1

If angle A and angle B form a linear pair, what is mangle A + mangle B?

feedback.text: A linear pair forms a straight angle, not necessarily a right angle.
Linear-pair angles are supplementary, so this sum is too small.
Correct. Angles that form a linear pair are supplementary.
A linear pair forms a straight angle, not a full rotation.

Question ID: GEO_U01_L08_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.6

Which counterexample disproves the claim All rectangles are squares?

feedback.text: A square is a rectangle and does not disprove the claim.

answer.text: A rectangle with side lengths 4 and 7

feedback.text: Correct. It is a rectangle but not a square.

answer.text: A triangle with three equal sides

feedback.text: A triangle is not a rectangle.
A circle is not a rectangle.
